company.name: Harborline Freight
company.summary: Harborline Freight is a road and sea freight forwarder based in Rotterdam, Netherlands. You and your team book container and truck transport for importers, handle customs paperwork, track shipments, and invoice clients. The company has about 85 employees across planning, customs, customer service, finance, sales, and warehouse.
offerings: Road freight forwarding for truck transport
Sea freight forwarding for container transport
company.customers: Importers that need container and truck transport into and through the Netherlands and Europe.

roles.title: Freight Planner
repetitive_tasks: Assign trucks and containers to loads
Update the TMS with route changes

roles.title: Customs Assistant
repetitive_tasks: Update the TMS with clearance status

roles.title: Customer Service Rep
repetitive_tasks: Log customer requests in the TMS

roles.title: Accounts Receivable Clerk
repetitive_tasks: Create client invoices from shipment data

strategy.situation: Harborline Freight runs road and sea freight forwarding from Rotterdam with about 85 staff across planning, customs, customer service, finance, sales, and warehouse. Most daily work runs through Outlook, Excel, a TMS, and Exact Online.
strategy.complication: Bookings, customs paperwork, shipment tracking, and billing still depend on people copying data between email, spreadsheets, and the TMS. As volumes rise, delays and errors show up in customer updates, declarations, and invoices.
strategy.governing_thought: Start with a shipment status agent, a customs declaration assistant, and an invoice matching agent to cut repetitive admin, speed customer answers, and free your team for exceptions.

key_arguments.headline: Planning, customs, customer service, and finance carry most of the repetitive admin
key_arguments.support: Shipment status questions, declaration preparation, and invoice matching repeat every day across four departments. These tasks follow clear rules and pull from systems you already use. They are also where small delays create customer complaints and billing disputes.

key_arguments.headline: Shipment status, customs drafts, and invoice matching give fast proof with low effort
key_arguments.support: Each of these three agents connects to Outlook and the TMS without replacing your core systems. Customs and invoice work keep a human approval step, so risk stays controlled. Customer service sees faster answers within weeks, which builds support for wider use.

key_arguments.headline: Start with human review, then expand to planning, sales, warehouse, and compliance
key_arguments.support: Run the first three agents with a named owner in each department and a daily review of outputs. Fix data gaps in the TMS before adding more connections. Once error rates and time savings hold, add planning, sales, carrier invoice, warehouse, and compliance agents in the same way.

strategy.executive_summary: Harborline Freight runs road and sea freight forwarding from Rotterdam with about 85 staff across planning, customs, customer service, finance, sales, and warehouse. Most daily work runs through Outlook, Excel, a TMS, and Exact Online. Bookings, customs paperwork, shipment tracking, and billing still depend on people copying data between email, spreadsheets, and the TMS. As volumes rise, delays and errors show up in customer updates, declarations, and invoices. Start with a shipment status agent, a customs declaration assistant, and an invoice matching agent to cut repetitive admin, speed customer answers, and free your team for exceptions.

maturity.label: Early piloting
maturity.note: You have core systems and practical Excel skills, but most repetitive work is still manual. A focused first wave of three agents can prove value before a wider rollout.

opportunities.title: Shipment status questions answered automatically
opportunities.description: The agent reads shipment status emails, checks the TMS and carrier tracking pages, and drafts a reply with the latest milestone. It also sends daily arrival notices and flags shipments with no update for more than 24 hours.

Rep opens TMS and carrier site
after: Agent reads email and matches shipment ID
Agent pulls latest status from TMS and carrier pages
Agent drafts reply with milestone and expected date
Human: Rep reviews and sends replies for exceptions
Agent sends arrival notices and flags missing updates

opportunities.title: Customs declarations prepared before review
opportunities.description: The agent collects invoices and packing lists from email, pulls shipment details from the TMS, and prepares a draft import declaration with suggested tariff codes. It checks the draft against past entries and submits only after a declarant approves.

Declarant opens TMS and customs portal
Declarant classifies goods and types declaration
after: Agent collects documents from email and TMS
Agent drafts declaration and suggests tariff codes

Agent logs clearance status in TMS

opportunities.title: Client invoices matched and prepared automatically
opportunities.description: The agent builds draft client invoices from TMS shipment data and rate agreements, then matches each invoice to the job file. It checks for missing charges and routes only unclear cases to billing staff.

Clerk checks rate agreement in Excel
Clerk creates invoice in Exact Online
Clerk matches invoice to job file
after: Agent pulls shipment data and rate agreement

Agent matches invoice to job file and flags missing charges

Agent posts approved invoices and updates tracker

roadmap.title: Prove three agents on everyday admin
items: Map shipment status emails, customs documents, and invoice data to TMS fields
Build the shipment status agent with a customer service review step
Build the customs declaration draft agent with declarant approval
Build the invoice matching agent with billing specialist review
Track time saved, reply speed, and error rates each week

roadmap.title: Connect planning, sales, and carrier invoice work
items: Add capacity request and rate comparison agent for planning
Add route change message agent for drivers and customers
Add carrier invoice matching agent for accounts payable
Add rate quote drafting agent for sales
Review results with department owners before moving on

roadmap.title: Extend to warehouse and compliance, then scale what works
items: Add inventory update agent for warehouse scan data
Add customs rule summary agent for compliance
Tune first three agents based on six months of use
Set a monthly review of accuracy, time saved, and staff feedback
Decide which agents to expand to more teams or lanes

risks.risk: Bad TMS data leads to wrong customer replies or invoices
risks.mitigation: Start with human review, add confidence flags, and clean key fields before each agent goes live.

risks.risk: Customs mistakes create fines or delayed clearance
risks.mitigation: Keep declarant approval before submission, limit tariff suggestions, and store an audit log of every draft.

risks.risk: Staff worry that agents will replace their jobs
risks.mitigation: Explain that agents handle repetitive steps, train people for exception handling, and share time saved with the team.

risks.risk: Carrier portals change or block automated access
risks.mitigation: Use email and TMS data first, add portal access only where allowed, and keep manual fallback steps documented.

risks.risk: Invoice errors hurt cash flow or client trust
risks.mitigation: Run sample checks for the first month, set approval thresholds, and review a weekly reconciliation report.
